subject: general
question:
Based on the situation in the sentence, choose the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

You cannot ______________ before replicating your successes and achievements multiple times; otherwise, people will deem your success a stroke of dumb luck.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"rest on your laurels"** means to be satisfied with your past achievements and to stop putting effort into improving or striving for more success. (अपने पिछले उपलब्धियों पर संतोष करना और आगे प्रयास न करना)

 
 
• **Example:** After winning the championship, the team decided not to rest on their laurels and began preparing for the next season.
 
 
 
• The sentence implies that one must consistently replicate their successes to avoid being considered lucky, which aligns with the meaning of "rest on your laurels."

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

__
 
• **Option 1: Play devil's advocate** (शैतान का वकील बनना): To argue against a point of view for the sake of debate or to explore the issue from different angles.

 
 
• **Example:** She played devil's advocate during the meeting to ensure that all possible problems were discussed.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Sit on the fence** (निर्णय लेने में झिझकना): To avoid taking sides in an argument or decision.
 
 
• **Example:** He always sits on the fence when it comes to political discussions.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Cut to the chase** (मुद्दे पर आना): To get to the point without wasting time.
 
 
• **Example:** Let's cut to the chase and discuss how we can improve sales this quarter.
